question: What architecture and Stellar standards should a team consider when tokenizing a regulated real-world asset?

golden.answer: Start with the legal claim, issuer/custodian, mint-and-burn controls, reserve attestations, transfer eligibility, and redemption process; the token does not make the off-chain asset trustworthy. A classic Stellar asset can use authorization-required, authorization-revocable, and clawback controls, while a Soroban token can encode richer compliance policies. SEP-41 is the common contract-token interface. SEP-56 is a Draft tokenized-vault interface for deposits, shares, and withdrawals—not a universal RWA attestation standard. Match SEP-6/24/31 only when fiat-ramp or cross-border anchor flows are part of the product.
keyFacts: Core RWA design covers legal claims, custody/reserve models, eligibility, and redemption.
Classic authorization/clawback or Soroban compliance can restrict regulated transfers.
Defines SEP-41 as a token interface.
Marks SEP-56 as a Draft tokenized-vault standard.
Excludes real-world attestation from SEP-56's scope.
avoid: SEP-56 proves that an off-chain asset exists and is fully reserved.
Issuing a token removes the need for custody, redemption, and securities-law analysis.
golden.notes: Status-sensitive details are stated as of 2026-07-11; grade later sourced changes leniently and require dated primary evidence.

corroboration.claim: The legal claim, custody or reserve model, eligibility controls, and redemption process are core parts of an RWA design.

evidence.note: Anchored-asset issuers publish anchor_asset, redemption_instructions ('Instructions to redeem your token for the underlying asset'), and attestation_of_reserve.
SEP-1 defines attestation_of_reserve, redemption_instructions, and the regulated (SEP-8) flag.
Tokenization relies on 'regulated financial institutions providing custody services'. The legal-claim element is a design principle, not a quoted line.

corroboration.claim: Classic asset authorization and clawback controls or Soroban compliance logic can restrict regulated transfers.

evidence.note: 'When AUTH_REQUIRED_FLAG is enabled, an issuer must approve an account before that account can hold its asset'; AUTH_REVOCABLE_FLAG lets an issuer freeze a trustline; clawback is documented on the same page.
Tokenization model comparison: Stellar Asset with issuer flags; SEP-41 contract tokens with custom logic; SEP-57 T-REX with built-in compliance rules.

corroboration.claim: SEP-41 is a token interface, while SEP-56 remains Draft and standardizes tokenized vault behavior rather than real-world attestation.

evidence.note: SEP-56 'Tokenized Vault Standard', Status Draft, Version 0.1.2; vaults take deposits and mint shares.
Official guide calls contract tokens SEP-41 implementations.

corroboration.claim: SEP-56 proves that an off-chain asset exists and is fully reserved.

evidence.note: Scope is deposits, withdrawals, and asset-to-share conversions; it defines no reserve or attestation mechanism.
Reserve attestation is a separate SEP-1 attestation_of_reserve URL field.

corroboration.claim: Issuing a token removes the need for custody, redemption, and securities-law analysis.

evidence.note: Anchored-token issuers still publish redemption instructions and reserve attestations.
Tokenization relies on regulated custody service providers.
